structured_output.hypothesis: Metacarpal breadth-to-length ratios of sheep and giraffe, relative to the ox, are about 2/3 and 1/3, and all the bone's breadth measurements scale by one common factor, so a single axial stretch relates the forms.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Compute R = (width/length of the taxon) / (width/length of Bos), using per-species mean metacarpal lengths and widths. Pass if R_sheep (Ovis) is 0.55–0.80 AND R_giraffe (Giraffa) is 0.25–0.42. For 'only difference', also require that the ratios of proximal width, midshaft width and distal width to length each give R within those same bands for each taxon, and that the three R values for a taxon differ by no more than 20% of their mean.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fail if R_sheep falls outside 0.55–0.80 or R_giraffe falls outside 0.25–0.42 for the midshaft-width ratio. Also fail if the proximal, midshaft and distal R values for either taxon differ by more than 20% of their mean, meaning the difference is not a single-axis stretch.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Cannon-bone' is the metacarpus (Thompson's figures show the fore cannon-bone). 'Breadth' maps to metacarpal proximal, midshaft and distal transverse width. 'Length' maps to maximum metacarpal length. 'Ox' maps to Bos taurus or a Bos/Bison relative if taurus is absent. 'Sheep' maps to Ovis aries or Ovis. 'Giraffe' maps to Giraffa camelopardalis. 'At equal length, X is 2/3 as broad' is read as a ratio of width/length indices, equivalent to a width-to-length shape ratio. This is a modern reinterpretation of Thompson's gridded outline comparison. Caveat: I did not confirm that the file lists these three taxa and measurements. The landing page does not show file contents, so the check must open raw_postcranial_measurements.xlsx first. If a taxon or measurement is missing, the test is undecidable on this dataset.

dataset.name: Predicting body mass in Ruminantia using postcranial measurements
dataset.publisher: Dryad (data by Alexa Wimberly, University of Chicago)
dataset.why_it_fits: The record holds 56 postcranial measurements from museum specimens of 101 extant ruminant species, with downloadable files. raw_postcranial_measurements.xlsx and body_mass_data.csv should give metacarpal length and proximal, midshaft and distal widths per species, which would let the width-to-length ratios be compared across Bos, Ovis and Giraffa. The page does not list the genera or the measurement columns, so I could not confirm that all three taxa are covered.
